lesson.title: The price cap limits rates, not your bill
body: Ofgem's energy price cap sets the most a supplier can charge per unit of gas and electricity (pence per kWh) and per day in standing charges, for people on standard variable tariffs. It is reviewed every three months.

The headline figure, such as £1,723 or the forecast £2,166, is what a 'typical' dual-fuel home paying by Direct Debit would pay over a year. Use more energy and you pay more; use less and you pay less. There is no upper limit on the total.

This time the two fuels are expected to move differently. Octopus says gas unit rates could rise by more than a third and electricity by less than a quarter. So a gas-heated home may see a bigger rise than the headline, while an all-electric one may see less.
lesson.takeaway: Work out your own change: multiply your yearly kWh (on your bill or app) by the new unit rates, then add 365 days of standing charge.

m365.title: Restore an older version of a file with Version history
m365.what: OneDrive and SharePoint keep earlier versions of Office files automatically. If someone overwrites a document or a sync goes wrong, you can roll back in a few clicks.
try: Open OneDrive or the SharePoint document library in your web browser.
Select the file, then choose the three dots (More actions) and pick 'Version history'.
Look through the list of versions with their dates and who changed them. Open one to check it.
Choose 'Restore' next to the version you want. It becomes the current version, and the newer one stays in the history.

explainer.story: Microsoft declares internal 'Code Red' after its 24-hour Microsoft 365 outage
bullets: The outage ran from about 4pm UK time on Thu 12 Nov to the next afternoon. Outlook was hit hardest, with Teams and Copilot also disrupted in around 74 countries (Al Jazeera, Downdetector).
Microsoft blamed a bug added in July to its networking gateway servers, which failed under extra traffic. Safeguards meant to contain it to one region also failed (BleepingComputer).
Reuters now reports an internal 'Code Red' to fix engineering and crisis-response gaps; some outlets say it targets one-hour recovery.
explainer.why: Many workplaces, including the NHS, run on Microsoft 365. It's a good moment to know how you would keep working if email and Teams went down for a day.

term.meaning: A promise from a provider about how reliable a service will be, usually as an uptime percentage, with credits or penalties if it falls short.
term.example: A 99.9% monthly uptime SLA allows about 43 minutes of downtime a month, so Microsoft's 24-hour outage was far outside that.
